  unless your task says so. Fixtures are built by scripts from real samples, never hand-invented payloads.
- Commit in small steps as work lands, message prefix "<task id>: ". Never rewrite history. Never commit secrets or .env.
- Never describe unbuilt work as done in README/docs. No numbers in docs except those generated into docs/FACTS.md.

TASK T60 · W4 · LLM client survives network errors
GOAL: A coordinator run ended after 4 turns with "LLM call failed: Connection error." The client retries only 429/5xx. Network on the
run host is flaky (DNS failures, connection resets), so the coordinator must ride through them.
READ: src/llm/client.ts (isRetryable, the retry loop, maxRetries, retryBaseMs), src/agent/coordinator.ts (how llm_error ends a run).
OWNS: src/llm/client.ts, src/agent/coordinator.ts (only how a transient LLM failure is handled), tests/llm-network.test.ts
BUILD: Treat connection errors (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, "Connection error", fetch failed, socket hang up) and
request timeouts as retryable, with up to 6 attempts and exponential backoff capped at 30 s plus jitter. If an LLM call still fails,
the coordinator saves state (it's resumable), records the error with the attempt count, and the CLI prints the exact resume command
(`roster run <repo> --run-id <id> --budget <usd>`).
ACCEPTANCE: tests with a fake transport: two connection errors then success → one result, three attempts; persistent failure → error
after 6 attempts and the resume hint printed. Whole suite green.
TEST: bun test tests/llm-network.test.ts && bun test && bun run typecheck
DO NOT TOUCH: anything outside OWNS.
